# browser CLI command reference

Drive real browsers with their profiles and cookies from the command line. Agents use a persistent task to navigate pages, inspect elements, interact with forms, capture screenshots and network traffic, then close the task. A local IPC service manages browser processes and tabs, using Chrome DevTools Protocol, Firefox WebDriver BiDi or native Arc control; tasks can also run on another machine over SSH.

Every `browser` command and subcommand, with its argument names and one-line description. Generated from the CLI's own command tree, so it never drifts from what `browser` registers.

- Full option lists live in [`command-index.json`](command-index.json); the searchable page is [`command-reference.html`](command-reference.html).
- `browser <command> --help` shows the help for one command.

_42 command groups · 65 commands._

## profiles: Manage browser profiles

```
browser profiles                     Manage browser profiles
browser profiles claim [name]        Move leftover central browser: profiles into this device's declaration file. Only profiles this machine can host are claimed; the rest stay central. Run on the machine that actually has the browser.
browser profiles create <name>       Create a new browser profile on this device
browser profiles doctor <name>       Diagnose a browser profile: where it is declared, binary, port, user-data-dir, onboarding state
browser profiles edit <name>         Edit an existing profile in place (stays in the store it already lives in)
browser profiles list                List all browser profiles and the devices declaring each one (WHERE)
browser profiles logins              Show which login-gated services each profile has a live session for, the account signed in, and whether login creds are available in the profile's secrets bundle (reads cookie/username presence only, never decrypts).
browser profiles prune               Remove dead profiles this device declares: browser not installed here, or never started
browser profiles remove <name>       Remove the profile alias and cached runtime dirs (never deletes native Arc data)
browser profiles rename <from> <to>  Rename a profile, moving its browser data with it (logins survive)
browser profiles seed                Create a machine-local profile for each installed browser (named <browser>-local), so you can pick or use one instead of hand-crafting each. Idempotent — existing profiles are left untouched.
browser profiles use [name]          Pick the profile `browser start` uses when no --profile is passed. No name opens a picker on a TTY or prints the current default headlessly.
browser profiles view <name>         View one profile
```

## prune: Close tabs for abandoned tasks — owning agent session exited, or idle past the window — and mark them done. The same reaper the daemon already runs every 5 minutes; use this to run it now.
_aliases: gc_

```
browser prune  Close tabs for abandoned tasks — owning agent session exited, or idle past the window — and mark them done. The same reaper the daemon already runs every 5 minutes; use this to run it now.
```

## record: Record a video of the page

```

```

## remote-control: Allow or deny other machines driving THIS machine's browser (`browser start --device <this-device>` or `agents ssh <this-device> browser …`). `on`/`off` to set (device-local, never synced); no argument prints the current value. Default off.

```
browser remote-control [state]  Allow or deny other machines driving THIS machine's browser (`browser start --device <this-device>` or `agents ssh <this-device> browser …`). `on`/`off` to set (device-local, never synced); no argument prints the current value. Default off.
```

## show: Open a URL or file for a human to read in browser.viewer (default: browser.profile), on the browser.device hub when one is set; reloads and focuses a tab already showing it; fails unless the viewer confirms it opened. Binds no task

```
browser show <url>  Open a URL or file for a human to read in browser.viewer (default: browser.profile), on the browser.device hub when one is set; reloads and focuses a tab already showing it; fails unless the viewer confirms it opened. Binds no task
```


## start: Start a browser task. Pass --profile <name>; omit to use your configured default (set it with `browser use <name>`). Page verbs (navigate/screenshot/…) create a task implicitly when none exists — start is for --profile/--url/--record/--title.

```
browser start  Start a browser task. Pass --profile <name>; omit to use your configured default (set it with `browser use <name>`). Page verbs (navigate/screenshot/…) create a task implicitly when none exists — start is for --profile/--url/--record/--title.
```
